extracted.intended_audience: Heads of executive departments and establishments; agency Deputy Directors, Directorate managers, planning/programming/budgeting officers, and comptrollers responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-44
extracted.subtask_description: Establish and run an Agency/Direcorate management improvement program per OMB Circular A-44 (Revised) including management-effectiveness actions, cost-reduction planning and reporting, validation, idea interchange, and awards/recognition. Includes required report formats, deadlines, and definitions of what counts as savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five interrelated program elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The management improvement program will consist of five interrelated elements: (1) Management effectiveness; (2) Cost reduction; (3) Idea interchange; (4) Presidential recognition of exceptional improvement actions; (5) Periodic study of Government-wide operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Circular 'sets forth policies, procedures, guidelines and responsibilities' for carrying out these elements and applies to all executive departments and agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual management improvement report covering the program elements will be prepared and submitted to the President through the Director of the Bureau of the Budget by September 30 of each year (first report due September 30, 1970).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must follow the requirements and definitions in Attachment A and include consolidated descriptions for Bureau of the Budget; agencies must submit required data in the prescribed format and meet intermediate agency deadlines (e.g., Directorate deadlines to Executive Director-Comptroller).

rubrics_metrics.name: Management effectiveness (selection and measurement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a formal management effectiveness program requiring identification of areas for study, establishment of objectives, selection of performance indicators, measurement of performance, and evaluation of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where performance cannot be reduced to dollars, develop coherent quantitative measurements where possible; otherwise devise qualitative or other informative techniques. Performance indicators should be selected to represent the combined effect of all management actions in the area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicators and measurement units
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance indicators will be expressed in quantitative standards (percentages, gross dollars, items, or other measures most appropriate for the area).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators are measures of performance; if existing data are insufficient, establish a new data base. Use base-period references (A = preceding fiscal year cumulative results; B = June 30 of preceding fiscal year status) and report base year, past year, and goals for each indicator (see Exhibit 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance evaluation content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise performance evaluation comparing actual performance against past experience and approved goals for each performance indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific actions contributing to improvement so other agencies may benefit, analyze shortfalls, indicate corrective actions initiated or required, and include target dates for completion or return to desired performance levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost reduction policy responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The head of each department/agency assumes personal responsibility for improving efficiency and economy; management at all levels must undertake vigorous efforts to improve procedures, eliminate nonessential activities/positions, and increase productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should seek to accomplish unprogrammed workload without additional staff by reassignment, improved manpower control, or other efficiency measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-reduction planning requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each department/agency head will prepare specific cost reduction plans that systematically identify and eliminate or curtail low priority and marginally effective activities; establish measurable objectives; and adopt less costly methods of achieving program objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should encourage innovation and ingenuity in developing new techniques for increasing productivity and set Directorate and component cost-reduction goals expressed in dollars and manpower where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary goal setting
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of each fiscal year department and agency heads will establish a cost reduction goal representing expected savings from new/improved management actions relative to the immediately preceding year's actual costs (or most appropriate recent costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to overall goals, agencies should set subgoals for major activities or organizational elements; goals must be realistic and represent actual expected savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of new vs improved management actions
rubrics_metrics.description: New management actions are internally conceived procedures/policies/innovations first applied by the reporting activity; improved management actions are changes to existing procedures/policies/techniques that reduce cost or increase revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to classify reported actions and compute monetary savings attributable to each action.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as monetary savings (inclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monetary savings reported must be the result of deliberate managerial actions taken to raise effectiveness or efficiency (reductions in costs or increases in revenues/fund availability attributable to new or improved management actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Savings must be calculated and reported separately for the past year and estimated for the next two fiscal years; planned expenditures or prior-year appropriations are used as the base for determining savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from monetary savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include as monetary savings reductions caused solely by decline in demand, deferment/postponement of programs, transfers of responsibility unless net Government saving, reductions due to uncompensated overtime, acquisition of excess property when funds would not have been available for new purchases, or reductions resulting from decisions by external authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also exclude reductions due solely to overestimates of budget needs; only deliberate internal management actions generate reportable savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and multi-year reporting of savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate monetary savings resulting from each action and report them for three fiscal years: the year action is taken and the next two succeeding fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-year savings represent funds made available and additional revenue resulting from actions; savings for succeeding years are estimates of resources that would have been required absent the actions. Reported past-year and estimated savings are dropped after each annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification, control, and disposition of savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish controls to assure funds made available by cost reduction actions are used only for approved programs, and identify disposition of savings using codes: (1) used to finance other approved requirements of the reporting unit; (2) reprogrammed to another appropriation or budget activity; (3) placed in reserve or applied to reducing the President's budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the anticipated use when savings are reprogrammed; identify current-year and budget-year effects so budget formulation can consider requirements that no longer exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of reported savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each department/agency must establish an internal system for validation — an independent evaluation of the reasonableness and validity of amounts reported as savings — with responsibility assigned to an organization independent of the claiming unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation should provide reasonable assurance that reported actions actually took place; savings reported are reasonable computations/estimates of savings occurring in the reported year and result from management actions; and reported savings are net of identifiable offsetting cost increases. The scope of validation should weigh cost of validation against potential benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-level validation responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of Planning, Programming, and Budgeting (or designated official) is responsible for validation of dollar/unit values of reported savings and reprogrammings before preparation of the Agency annual report to OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation consists of reviewing an adequate number of individual savings actions to confirm accuracy and disposition/allocation to approved programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea interchange and external dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must have an internal system for distributing management improvement information to its organizational elements and identify in its annual report actions considered applicable to other departments/agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions submitted for external distribution should be concise, include the action, methodology used, new approaches or techniques, and a point of contact; the Bureau of the Budget will consolidate and distribute applicable items to all agencies. Screen items for relevance and consider security/need-to-know factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives and recognition systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should employ techniques (award ceremonies, certificates, letters, publicity, symposiums, workshops, money rewards via Incentive Awards Program) to stimulate improvement actions and motivate personnel at all levels to innovate and report actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives are to cause innovative thinking, action on ideas, and reporting of actions; agencies may nominate individuals and organizational units for Presidential recognition with detailed descriptions of efforts and results for review by the President's Advisory Council on Management Improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic Government-wide studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodically the Bureau of the Budget will choose a common operational area for Government-wide study and establish an interagency steering group to coordinate the effort and write a final report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency management should focus on selected areas and submit reports on accomplishments including dollar savings, management actions taken, and plans for future improvements; possible study areas include common administrative functions such as records management, travel, communications, printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directorate plan and report structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Directorate's annual plan/report must include four sections: Section I — Management Effectiveness Goals (upcoming FY); Section II — Cost-Reduction Goals (upcoming FY); Section III — Management Effectiveness Accomplishments (current FY); Section IV — Cost-Reduction Accomplishments (current FY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section II should set forth Directorate and component cost-reduction goals in dollars and manpower; Section III and IV report achievements vs prior planning goals and include unanticipated achievements and incentive awards recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-reduction narrative and summary recap
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual reporting must include a narrative statement (general summary, specific actions taken, productivity progress, reductions in manpower, problems needing higher-level assistance) and a summary recap of savings containing descriptions of areas, monetary savings goals, estimated budgetary effect, actual monetary savings achieved, proposed disposition of anticipated savings, and reductions in authorized positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach supporting data and complete the reporting format as prescribed (Exhibit 1), providing minimum data items listed for recap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls on reporting and budget integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Savings must be reported by component, program category, sub-category and element, and the estimated budgetary impact of cost-reduction actions must be incorporated in the annual budget submission as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the current-year and budget-year effect of actions so budget formulation and review processes account for requirements that no longer exist; establish controls to assure savings are used only for approved programs or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and internal deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Directorates must submit plans/reports on schedules set by the Agency (e.g., by 30 June each year to Executive Director-Comptroller; initial agency plan for FY 1971 by 31 December 1970; incentive award recommendations by 31 July each year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to internal submission deadlines to allow consolidation, validation, and timely submission to the Bureau of the Budget/OMB; designate senior officers as contact points for management improvement matters.
